records.name: Code-as-Data Representation
records.definition: The requirement that a program's code be representable in the same data structures the language manipulates.

records.name: Macro Systems
records.definition: A facility that lets code transform other code at compile time by operating on its data representation.

records.name: Opaque Syntax Trees
records.definition: Syntax trees a program cannot inspect or manipulate as data, so code cannot be transformed programmatically.

records.name: AST or Data Representation
records.definition: The requirement that code be represented as a structured syntax tree or data rather than as raw text.

records.name: Program Transformation
records.definition: The ability to analyze and rewrite a program by manipulating its structured representation.

records.name: Safety/Debuggability
records.definition: The degree to which treating code as manipulable data can obscure what runs and make it harder to debug.

records.name: String-Based Code Generation
records.definition: Building code by concatenating strings, so the result is unchecked, injection-prone, and hard to analyze.

records.name: Boilerplate Elimination
records.definition: The ability to remove repetitive boilerplate by generating it from a single declaration.

records.name: Explicit Handwritten Code
records.definition: Writing code out by hand explicitly rather than generating it, favoring directness and debuggability over reuse.

records.name: Reflection/AST/Code Generation
records.definition: The requirement that a language expose reflection, syntax trees, or code generation for programs to manipulate themselves.

records.name: Performance/Safety
records.definition: The degree to which inspecting and dispatching on types at runtime costs performance and bypasses static safety.

records.name: Runtime Type Metadata
records.definition: Type information retained at runtime so a program can inspect the shape of its own values.

records.name: Diagnostics
records.definition: The ability to inspect a running system's own structure and state to diagnose it.

records.name: Self-Describing Systems
records.definition: The degree to which a system carries enough metadata to describe its own structure and capabilities at runtime.

records.name: Build Complexity
records.definition: The degree to which moving work into the build to run at compile time makes the build harder to set up and reason about.

records.name: Compile-Time Inputs
records.definition: The requirement that the inputs a computation needs be known at compile time so it can run then.

records.name: Early Error Detection
records.definition: The ability to catch errors at compile time rather than letting them surface at runtime.

records.name: Runtime Dynamic Evaluation
records.definition: Evaluating code or expressions dynamically at runtime, trading compile-time checking for runtime flexibility.

records.name: Dynamic Optimization/Adaptation
records.definition: The ability to generate specialized code at runtime to optimize or adapt to observed conditions.

records.name: Safe Generation Boundary
records.definition: The requirement that runtime code generation be confined to a safe, sandboxed boundary away from untrusted input.

records.name: Security/Debugging
records.definition: The degree to which generating and running code at runtime widens the attack surface and complicates debugging.

records.name: Domain Expressiveness
records.definition: The ability to express domain rules directly in terms a domain expert recognizes.

records.name: Formal Grammar/Semantics
records.definition: The requirement that a domain language have a defined grammar and semantics rather than an ad-hoc syntax.

records.name: General-Purpose Boilerplate
records.definition: Expressing domain logic through verbose general-purpose code and its boilerplate instead of a concise domain notation.

records.name: Tooling/Maintenance
records.definition: The degree to which owning a custom language burdens a team with building and maintaining its tooling.

records.name: Code Generation or Interpreters
records.definition: The requirement that a domain language be backed by a generator or interpreter that executes it.

records.name: Domain Modeling
records.definition: Expressing a problem domain as a first-class language of its own concepts and rules.

records.name: High-Level Domain Expression
records.definition: The ability to express solutions in high-level domain terms rather than low-level general-purpose code.

records.name: One-Size General-Purpose Code
records.definition: Expressing every domain in a single general-purpose language, rather than in domain-specific notations.

records.name: Toolchain Complexity
records.definition: The degree to which building custom languages adds compilers, parsers, and editors to a project's toolchain.

records.name: Formal Model
records.definition: A precise, machine-processable model of a system from which implementations are generated.

records.name: Generated Implementations
records.definition: Implementation code produced automatically from a model rather than written by hand.

records.name: Handwritten Divergence
records.definition: Hand-editing generated code so it drifts from the model it came from, breaking regeneration.

records.name: Transformation Rules
records.definition: The requirement that explicit rules define how a model maps to generated implementation code.

records.name: Syntax Tree Generation
records.definition: A technique for generating code by building and printing a syntax tree instead of concatenating strings.

records.name: Reflective Contract Bypass
records.definition: A defect in which reflection is used to reach members that a type's contract or visibility hides.

records.name: Deferred Static Check
records.definition: A defect in which a check or generation that could run at compile time is repeated at runtime.

records.name: Ad-Hoc Mini-Language
records.definition: A defect in which rules are written in an informal mini-language that has no grammar and no validator.
